summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 was fast but narrow: the supplied closeout timing reports 10 minutes of wall time for 2 completed experiments, averaging 5 minutes each. The critical path was dominated by the arXiv Bundle v10 gate after exp1269 critical paper fixes. GPU capacity was unused, but no zombie GPU processes were present. Pre-flight checks were measured in seconds, not minutes; the main remaining efficiency gain is better parallel scheduling and keeping docs/manual upload work off the critical path.
timing_scope_note: Primary totals use the task-provided timing block for the 10-minute operational closeout slice. Repository artifacts also show broader .99 milestone activity; this retro is intentionally scoped to the supplied operational timing data.

slowest_experiments.title: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: This sat on the publication critical path: exp1270 could only run after exp1269 fixed the five paper-critical measured-claim issues, then it compiled and bundled the paper. The repo artifact confirms pdf_compiled=true, bundle_path written, and arxiv_submitted=false.

slowest_experiments.title: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10
slowest_experiments.why_long: Not actually slow. It appears in the supplied slowest list because the milestone slice contained only two completed items; docs reconciliation was effectively a no-op in wall-clock terms.

bottlenecks_identified: The publication lane was serialized: exp1270 was correctly gated on exp1269, so the longest item consumed the full 10-minute wall time.
GPU utilization was inefficient at the milestone closeout. Both RTX 3090s were at 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization, with no GPU processes.
No gpu_monitor.py-class zombie processes were wasting material resources. The monitor reported an empty process list and no warnings.
Pre-flight was not a bottleneck in this slice. Conductor rows for exp1269 and exp1270 show 81 tests passing with one warning in 8.24s and 7.89s.
Doc reconciliation was efficient for the arXiv lane, but it still ran in-process on the critical path instead of being batched after terminal artifacts.
Manual publication closeout remains split from bundle creation: exp1270 compiled the PDF and wrote the tarball, but arxiv_submitted=false.
The milestone slice underused available parallelism. While exp1270 depended on exp1269, independent CPU/GPU tasks from the broader .99 plan could have run while the publication lane executed.
improvements_suggested: Keep exp1269-style critical paper fixes and exp1270 bundle creation as a single supervised publication lane, but launch independent non-publication tasks in parallel.
Cache TeX dependencies and add a deterministic arxiv-bundle make/check target that emits compile_minutes, bundle_path, and upload_pending_reason.
Promote gpu_monitor.py suggestions into scheduler decisions: when both GPUs are idle and GPU tasks are queued, start a DualGPURunner lane instead of advancing only CPU/docs work.
Run pre-flight once per milestone activation when the working tree is unchanged, then let low-risk docs/bundle tasks reuse the result.
Batch changelog and roadmap reconciliation after terminal artifacts exist; keep in-process docs off the critical path unless the artifact itself requires them.
Record gate_wait_minutes separately from compile_minutes so future retros can distinguish legitimate dependency time from tooling overhead.
Add an explicit manual-upload checklist artifact for arXiv submission, separate from compiled-bundle success, so upload-pending state is not confused with execution failure.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: The exact two-experiment slice cannot be reduced much below the exp1269 to exp1270 dependency chain, but the next milestone could plausibly save about 30% wall time by overlapping independent CPU/GPU lanes, caching TeX/pre-flight work, and moving docs/manual upload reconciliation out of the critical path.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Start an independent GPU lane whenever gpu_monitor.py reports both GPUs idle and queued GPU work exists.
Make arXiv bundle generation a cached deterministic target with separate gate, compile, bundle, and upload-pending timings.
Batch ops docs reconciliation after terminal artifacts instead of running it inline during the critical path.

gpu_utilization.assessment: Not compute-efficient at the milestone level. The completed publication tasks did not need GPUs, but the machine had two idle RTX 3090s that could have handled independent queued GPU work in parallel.

zombie_process_assessment.basis: scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json reported processes=[], warnings=[], and only 4 MB allocated on each GPU at 0% utilization.
zombie_process_assessment.note: There was no evidence of zombie VRAM waste; the issue was idle capacity.

preflight_assessment: Not a bottleneck. The relevant conductor rows show focused pre-flight/test checks of 8.24s and 7.89s, which are negligible against 10 minutes of wall time.
doc_reconciliation_assessment: Efficient in raw time because the in-process docs pass was reported as 0 minutes, but still better handled as a batched post-artifact step so it never sits on a critical publication lane.
parallelization_assessment: The direct exp1269 to exp1270 gate was not parallelizable, but the broader .99 plan contained independent CPU, docs, WOPR, and GPU-eligible tasks. Those could have run beside the publication lane, especially while both GPUs were idle.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: exp1270 arXiv Bundle v10 took the full reported 10 minutes because it was gated on exp1269 critical fixes and then performed compile/bundle publication work. The docs pass was listed at 0 minutes and was not a real bottleneck.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No at the milestone level. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout. The completed arXiv tasks were CPU/docs tasks, but independent GPU work could have been scheduled concurrently.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes: No. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings; the 4 MB per GPU allocation was negligible context residue.
question_answers.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: The exp1269 to exp1270 dependency itself could not be parallelized, but independent .99 tasks could have run in parallel with the publication lane.
question_answers.was_the_pre_flight_test_suite_a_bottlene: No. The relevant checks took under 9 seconds each.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Mostly yes for this slice, since docs were reported at 0 minutes. They should still be batched after terminal artifacts to avoid critical-path coupling.
question_answers.what_tooling_would_speed_up_the_next_mil: GPU-aware parallel scheduling, cached TeX/pre-flight targets, structured gate/compile timing fields, batched docs reconciliation, and a separate manual-upload checklist artifact.

meta_reflection: The milestone was not slow in absolute terms; it was narrow and serial. The next operational improvement is not longer prompts or larger budgets. It is scheduling discipline: isolate the unavoidable publication dependency, then keep the GPUs and independent CPU lanes busy while that dependency resolves.
